claims.text: Combining SQS-based configurational-disorder sampling, anharmonic lattice dynamics, and machine-learning corrections will improve predictions of phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed approach will reduce prediction error by approximately 25% relative to conventional DFT-based models.
The predicted improvement applies to uniformly disordered, single-phase high-entropy alloys.
Prediction accuracy will deteriorate for samples containing precipitates or phase segregation.
Multi-element mass fluctuations enhance phonon scattering.
Multi-element force-constant fluctuations enhance phonon scattering.
Chemical disorder produces localization of acoustic phonon modes.
Explicitly incorporating chemical disorder into lattice dynamics captures the effect of disorder on phonon lifetimes.
Refining force-constant distributions produces more accurate thermal-conductivity predictions.
The approach will capture nonlinear temperature-dependent effects of disorder-induced phonon scattering between approximately 300 and 600 K.
Conventional DFT and limited machine-learning models inadequately represent disorder-induced phonon scattering.
The approach is primarily applicable under equilibrium conditions to homogeneous, single-phase high-entropy alloys.
The approach may lose accuracy under conditions far from equilibrium.
The magnitude of the accuracy improvement may depend on the degree of disorder and the alloy composition.
Experimental calibration is required to refine the estimated quantitative performance gain.
Failure to achieve at least a 25% reduction in prediction error relative to conventional DFT is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.
Significant disagreement between predicted and measured phonon lifetimes or thermal conductivities is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.
